findings.description: GUARD_PATTERNS defined but never used. The is_guarded function delegates to engines.guard.is_guarded which has its own more comprehensive GUARD_PATTERNS. This dead code could cause confusion if someone updates one but not the other.

STOP_FILE uses hardcoded '/tmp/browser-agent-stop' while engines/guard.py uses RUN_DIR (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or /tmp)/browser-agent for TAKEOVER_FILE and APPROVAL_FILE. Inconsistent runtime directories could cause confusion in multi-user or containerized environments.

Site allow feature (site_allow_check, remember_site_allow, forget_site_allow, SITE_ALLOW_FILE) is fully implemented but never called from is_guarded or anywhere else. The comment at line 84-88 describes integration with guard logic but it's not hooked up. This appears to be extra scope beyond the stated intent (which mentions grants but not site-level 'always allow').

RUN_DIR is created with chmod 0o700 but the files created within it (TAKEOVER_FILE, APPROVAL_FILE, SITE_ALLOW_FILE) inherit default permissions (typically 0o644 world-readable). While the content is low-sensitivity (action IDs, timestamps, domain allowlists), explicit chmod 0o600 on file creation would be more consistent with the directory protection.

element_facts catches all exceptions (Exception) and returns None for fail-closed behavior. This is intentional per the comment but could mask programming errors (e.g., typos in CDP method names). The broad catch is acceptable for a fail-closed security boundary but worth noting.

OPAQUE_TARGET regex (r'^\s*(bid\s*[:=]\s*)?\d+\s*$') does not match 'bid 1' (space separator without colon/equals). However, decide_llm.py normalizes all numeric targets to 'bid:N' format (line 90-92), so this only matters if actions come from an untrusted/unnormalized source. The guard's fail-closed design means unrecognized formats are guarded anyway.

testing_summary: Reviewed test files for coverage of guard logic, grants, element classification, and decide_llm validation. Tests use fake models/pages and monkeypatch shared state; no browser integration tests exist (expected for unit tests).
risk_rationale: The change correctly implements the three stated goals: fixes the import order, adds real element classification with fail-closed typing guards, and introduces single-use action-bound grants to prevent double-gating. No authorization bypasses or privacy leaks found. The issues are minor dead code, inconsistent temp paths, and an unused site-allow feature.
